prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale:ground-only land/coastal/cryosphere imagery;predictable latency,documented quality,retained external interfaces. Mission Control Center(Bluebell/local voice):safety,commands,passes,anomalies,routing,handover. Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral/legacy logs):navigation,maneuvers,orbit/visibility/pointing→planning. Mission Planning System(Cedar):authoritative observation/contact timelines,booking requests(service,antenna,elevation,volume,priority),constraints→plans. Network Control System(Lantern):authoritative circuits/routing/allocations/readiness/contact records;antenna/link/timing/routing status→Bluebell. Ground Network Manager(Juniper/rosters):assignments,availability,conflicts,maintenance,staffing,site coordination;must confirm maintenance compatibility before command preparation. Antenna Deicing Notice:mandatory maintenance-critical pre-acquisition tasks;Spacecraft Operations Team assesses contingency contact margin. North S-Band Antenna(nominal),South S-Band Antenna(procedure-compatible alternate):commands/low-rate telemetry→Bluebell;Kiruna X-Band Antenna,Svalbard X-Band Antenna:high-volume downlink opportunities. Schedules cover imaging,recorder management,housekeeping,antenna support. Cedar flags spacecraft/station/staffing conflicts;checks slew,sun-angle,power,thermal recovery,recorder capacity,command-load size,incompatible-activity separation;converged command preparation package→Bluebell command engineering. Command Validation Gateway(Osprey):mandatory independent pre-uplink validation before operational approval;checks syntax,timing,parameter ranges,sequencing,mode compatibility,approved baseline;rejects unapproved edits,missing provenance,expired configuration references,out-of-authority-window activities. Telemetry Ingest Service:latest state→command-assumption checks;frames/contact/flow indicators→operations/engineering/processing;validates framing/time continuity,records metadata,separates gaps/interruptions;produces Pass Replay Packet. Orbit Determination Engine:tracking→orbital solution/state,visibility,maneuver/pointing/time-tagged-event/observation geometry;qualified-pass Doppler Residual Report. Payload Processing Facility(Forgehouse/console discussions/shift logs):processing,calibration,distribution;receives planning metadata,not product-delivery commitments. Primary Processing Cluster(nominal),Backup Processing Cluster(controlled failover):planning checks routine capacity only. Product Quality Service:pre-distribution checks;geometry/mode quality

New part:
S125: The Cybersecurity Desk reviews command preparation exceptions when unusual access, emergency procedure use, or nonstandard transfer paths are requested before uplink.
S126: Final approval requires concurrence from the Mission Control Center and the Spacecraft Operations Team before any command stack is placed in the queue for the next authorized uplink opportunity.
S127: After final command approval, orbit state management remains under continuous control so that operations users work from a common predicted trajectory.
S128: The Orbit Determination Engine fits dynamic orbit solutions using radiometric tracking, spacecraft telemetry timing, force models, and the latest approved maneuver history.
S129: Tracking arcs include measurements associated with the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna when those data meet quality and timing criteria.
S130: The Product Quality Service checks each orbit solution for frame consistency, covariance reasonableness, time-tag continuity, and agreement with recent contact predictions.
S131: The Flight Dynamics Team uses the residual report to separate station-related tracking biases from dynamic model errors before accepting an orbit solution.
S132: The Flight Dynamics Facility maintains the authoritative orbit catalog for the ground segment and records the modeling assumptions applied to each accepted solution.
S133: Maneuver screening evaluates orbit maintenance options against fuel use, ground contact visibility, payload outage constraints, and post-burn tracking opportunities.
S134: For each candidate burn, the Flight Dynamics Team computes expected state change, execution tolerance, recovery strategy, and the earliest time when the solution can be declared stable.
S135: Collision assessment uses externally supplied conjunction data together with the current covariance to estimate miss distance, encounter geometry, and probability of collision.
S136: The Flight Dynamics Team maintains screening rules that distinguish routine catalog monitoring from events requiring immediate operator notification.
S137: If the predicted risk exceeds the mission threshold, the Spacecraft Operations Team receives a maneuver recommendation package that includes timing constraints and operational impacts.
S138: Attitude geometry support translates the predicted orbit into Sun angle, Earth limb, lunar exclusion, target visibility, and antenna pointing information for daily operations.
S139: The Flight Dynamics Facility sends the Star Tracker Mask File after verifying predicted bright-object exclusions against the current attitude plan.
S140: Bluebell requires that each flight dynamics delivery include a validity interval, coordinate frame, generation time, and operational use statement.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
